summary: Every nested entry must be examined and every integer must be yielded, so the explicit-stack traversal matches the linear input-and-output lower bound.

optimality.argument: Let N count integer entries and nested-array entries across the recursive structure. Any entry may be an integer to yield or an array containing further integers, so a correct complete traversal must inspect all N entries. The reference processes each entry once and performs constant stack work per array frame, giving O(N) total time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Skipping any recursive entry can omit either that integer or integers stored inside that nested array, establishing an Omega(N) inspection bound.
Each entry advances exactly one frame index once, and each nested array pushes and pops one frame, for O(N) total operations.
Authored cases compare against independent recursive flattening across empty, flat, deep, asymmetric, duplicate, zero-valued, and all-empty structures.
